implementation.name: JTBIOCOM
implementation.notes: Source availability (T5.4): open -- the HDL lives in the jotego/jtcores monorepo at cores/biocom/, 8 source files. There is no open_source column in the delivered schema (data-model.md §1.9 deleted the proposed core table together with its flags); the presence of hdl_language_id, license_id and implementation_path rows is how that fact is stated here. License: https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/blob/master/LICENSE is the verbatim GPLv3 text, and the per-file grant in https://github.com/jotego/jtcores/blob/master/cores/biocom/hdl/jtbiocom_bus.v reads "either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version" -- hence GPL-3.0-or-later. Machine mapping: 7 MRA files in jotego/jtbin's mra/ directory name <rbf>jtbiocom</rbf>; 1 setnames resolved exactly to a MAME 0.288 machine and 6 through MAME's own cloneof relation to the parent that survives extract/machine.json's parents-only filter, giving 1 distinct machine_id rows. hdl_language_id: 8 of 8 HDL files are verilog (8 verilog), excluding the shared framework directory. accuracy_id omitted: jotego's README claims faithfulness in prose but states no timing-fidelity level this build could check against data/lookup/accuracy_level.json. Dependency deliberately not recorded: cores/biocom/cfg/files.yaml pulls jttora_obj.v and jttora_objdata.v from cores/tora/hdl, but no implementation_dependency row is written in that direction. Those two headers read Date: 1-12-2022 and Date: 1-1-2023, while this core's own jtbiocom_main.v and jtbiocom_mcu.v read Date: 12-9-2019 and Date: 14-9-2019: the object engine was written three years later, during Tiger Road work, and both cores were then pointed at it. The shared thing is that object engine, not the JTTORA core. The real core-level derivation runs the other way -- JTTORA reuses this core's 68000 main section and 8751 MCU -- and that is the edge that is recorded, on jttora.
